newsitem.title: USA: GM forges marketing relationship with Disney.
newsitem.headline: GM forges marketing relationship with Disney.

text.p: Visitors to Walt Disney World's new Test Track thrill ride will get a heavy sales pitch from General Motors Corp. with their fun, and the automaker and Disney said Friday the Epcot attraction was only the first of several marketing ties between them.

Test Track opens this spring and replaces the "General Motors World of Motion" exhibit at Disney World's Epcot Centre in Orlando, Fla. The multimillion dollar attraction attempts to recreate the rigours and thrill of driving prototype vehicles on a high-speed proving ground track.
Guests are then subjected to a marketing pitch that includes simulated auto show-style unveilings of GM vehicles and information about GM safety and quality efforts.
GM also is tying the launch of its Chevrolet Venture minivan with the promotional effort for Disney's "Hercules" animated film and will participate in a mall tour for the movie this spring.
The tour is expected to hit major malls in 22 cities and is expected to expose both the film and the minivan to about 4 million people.
"You can expect to see many marketing initiatives growing out of this architecture," said GM North American advertising chief Philip Guarascio.

He said the automaker will benefit from its association with the Walt Disney Co. because the entertainment and theme park giant has the ability to engage people and put them into a "positive frame of mind."
